title: VLAN Connectivity Issue - Server Unreachable
symptom: PC gets an IP address but cannot reach the server in VLAN 30. The PC can ping its default gateway.
topology_note: PC connected to Switch1 Fa0/2 (VLAN 10). Switch1 trunk to Router1 Fa0/0. Server in VLAN 30 on Switch1 Fa0/5.
show_output:
show vlan brief
VLAN Name Status Ports
10 Data active Fa0/2
30 Servers active Fa0/5

switchport access vlan 30 command missing on Fa0/5 - port shows VLAN 1
show interfaces trunk
Port Mode Encapsulation Status Native vlan
Fa0/1 on 802.1q trunking 1
expected_fault: Server port not assigned to correct VLAN (still in default VLAN 1)

title: Default Gateway Misconfiguration
symptom: PC can ping other devices on the same subnet but cannot reach any remote network.
topology_note: PC connected to Switch1, Switch1 uplinks to Router1 which routes between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20.
show_output:
show ip interface brief
FastEthernet0/0 192.168.10.1 YES manual up up
PC ipconfig: IP 192.168.10.50 Gateway 192.168.20.1
expected_fault: PC configured with wrong default gateway (points to a different subnet)

title: DHCP Pool Exhaustion
symptom: New PCs on VLAN 20 fail to obtain an IP address; existing PCs work fine.
topology_note: Router1 configured as DHCP server for VLAN 20 (192.168.20.0/27).
show_output:
show ip dhcp pool VLAN20
Pool VLAN20 :
 Utilization mark high = 100 %
 Total addresses = 30
 Leased addresses = 30
 Pending event = none
expected_fault: DHCP pool exhausted - no free addresses left in the scope

title: DNS Resolution Failure
symptom: Users can ping the web server by IP address but cannot browse to it using its hostname.
topology_note: PC on VLAN 10, DNS server configured as 8.8.8.8 in the DHCP scope but internal DNS is 192.168.10.5.
show_output:
ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 8.8.8.8
nslookup intranet.local
*** 8.8.8.8 can't find intranet.local: Non-existent domain
expected_fault: PC is using an external DNS server that has no record for the internal hostname

title: Missing Static Route Between Sites
symptom: HQ site cannot reach Branch site subnet 172.16.20.0/24, but the WAN link is up.
topology_note: R1 (HQ) <-> Serial link <-> R2 (Branch). R2 LAN = 172.16.20.0/24.
show_output:
show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set
C 172.16.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
C 10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
(No route to 172.16.20.0/24)
expected_fault: Missing static/dynamic route for the branch LAN subnet on HQ router

title: ACL Blocking Legitimate Traffic
symptom: Users in VLAN 10 cannot access the file server in VLAN 30 even though routing is correctly configured.
topology_note: Router1 has an inbound ACL on the VLAN 30 SVI.
show_output:
show access-lists
Extended IP access list BLOCK_VLAN10
 10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any
 20 permit ip any any (0 matches)
expected_fault: Overly broad deny statement in ACL blocks all VLAN 10 traffic to VLAN 30

title: NAT Overload Not Translating Outbound Traffic
symptom: Internal hosts cannot reach the internet; internal-to-internal traffic works fine.
topology_note: Router1 connects internal LAN (192.168.1.0/24) to ISP via Serial0/1/0.
show_output:
show ip nat translations
(empty)
show run | include nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface Serial0/1/0 overload
(interface GigabitEthernet0/0 missing 'ip nat inside')
expected_fault: Inside interface not marked with 'ip nat inside', so NAT overload never triggers

title: Wireless Client Cannot Associate with AP
symptom: Laptop detects the SSID 'CorpWiFi' but fails to connect, showing 'incorrect password' repeatedly even with the correct passphrase.
topology_note: AP1 broadcasts SSID CorpWiFi using WPA2-PSK, connected to Switch1 access port.
show_output:
AP1 config: authentication WPA2 PSK ascii CorpPass123
Client security profile: WPA2-Enterprise selected on laptop instead of WPA2-Personal
expected_fault: Client wireless profile mismatched security type (Enterprise vs Personal/PSK)

title: Duplicate IP Address Conflict
symptom: Two PCs on VLAN 10 intermittently lose connectivity; Windows shows 'IP address conflict' popup on one machine.
topology_note: Static IP assigned on PC-A (192.168.10.20), DHCP scope on same subnet also includes .20 in its range.
show_output:
show ip dhcp conflict
IP address Detection method Detection time
192.168.10.20 Ping Mon Mar 10 09:15:20
expected_fault: Statically assigned address overlaps with DHCP scope range, causing duplicate IP conflict

title: Incorrect Subnet Mask Causing Isolated Host
symptom: One PC on VLAN 10 cannot communicate with any other device, even those on the same VLAN.
topology_note: VLAN 10 subnet is 192.168.10.0/24. PC statically configured.
show_output:
ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 192.168.10.55
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.192
Default Gateway: 192.168.10.1
expected_fault: Subnet mask misconfigured (/26 instead of /24) places host and gateway on different logical subnets

title: Trunk Native VLAN Mismatch
symptom: Intermittent connectivity issues and CDP native VLAN mismatch warnings appear in switch logs between two switches.
topology_note: Switch1 and Switch2 connected via a trunk link (Gi0/1 on both).
show_output:
Switch1: show interfaces trunk -> Native vlan: 1
Switch2: show interfaces trunk -> Native vlan: 99
%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch between trunk ports on Switch1 and Switch2

title: Interface Administratively Down
symptom: An entire branch office lost connectivity after a maintenance window.
topology_note: R2 WAN interface Serial0/0/0 connects branch to HQ.
show_output:
show ip interface brief
Serial0/0/0 10.0.0.2 YES manual administratively down down
expected_fault: WAN interface was left administratively shut down after maintenance

title: Missing VLAN on Trunk Allowed List
symptom: New VLAN 40 (Guest) created for a project, but guest devices cannot reach the guest DHCP server on the other switch.
topology_note: Switch1 and Switch2 connected via trunk Gi0/2. VLAN 40 created on both switches.
show_output:
show interfaces trunk
Port Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/2 1,10,20,30
expected_fault: VLAN 40 not included in the trunk's allowed VLAN list

title: Router-on-a-Stick Subinterface Misconfigured
symptom: Inter-VLAN routing fails for VLAN 30 only; VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 route correctly.
topology_note: Router1 Gi0/0 has subinterfaces Gi0/0.10, Gi0/0.20, Gi0/0.30 for router-on-a-stick.
show_output:
show run interface Gi0/0.30
encapsulation dot1Q 3
ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: Subinterface encapsulation uses wrong dot1Q VLAN tag (3 instead of 30)

title: DHCP Relay (ip helper-address) Missing
symptom: Devices in VLAN 20 do not receive an IP address; DHCP server is centralized in VLAN 10.
topology_note: Router1 has SVI for VLAN 20; central DHCP server sits in VLAN 10 at 192.168.10.5.
show_output:
show run interface vlan20
interface Vlan20
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
(no ip helper-address statement present)
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on VLAN 20 SVI to relay DHCP requests to the central server

title: Access Port Configured as Trunk
symptom: PC connected to Switch1 Fa0/8 cannot obtain an IP address and receives a 169.254.x.x address.
topology_note: Fa0/8 intended as a simple access port for a single PC.
show_output:
show interfaces switchport Fa0/8
Administrative Mode: trunk
Operational Mode: trunk
expected_fault: Port accidentally configured as a trunk instead of access, blocking normal DHCP/broadcast behaviour

title: Wrong DNS Server Pushed by DHCP
symptom: All PCs in VLAN 10 fail to resolve internal hostnames after a DHCP scope change.
topology_note: Router1 DHCP pool VLAN10 was recently edited by an admin.
show_output:
show run | section ip dhcp pool VLAN10
network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
default-router 192.168.10.1
dns-server 203.0.113.5
expected_fault: DHCP pool pushes an incorrect external DNS server instead of the internal DNS server (192.168.10.5)

title: Asymmetric Routing Causing Dropped Return Traffic
symptom: Ping from Branch to HQ server succeeds but the HTTP session to the same server times out.
topology_note: Dual WAN links between Branch and HQ; static routes configured differently on each router.
show_output:
R1 show ip route -> 172.16.20.0/24 via Serial0/0/0
R2 show ip route -> 172.16.10.0/24 via Serial0/1/0
(return path uses a different link than outbound, ACL on Serial0/1/0 blocks established TCP)
expected_fault: Asymmetric routing combined with a stateful-like ACL on the return path drops mid-session TCP packets

title: ACL Applied to Wrong Interface Direction
symptom: Internal users cannot reach the internet even though the NAT and ACL rules look correct on paper.
topology_note: ACL 101 meant to filter outbound internet traffic on Serial0/1/0.
show_output:
show run interface Serial0/1/0
ip access-group 101 in
(ACL 101 was designed for traffic leaving the router, should be applied 'out' or reversed)
expected_fault: ACL applied in the wrong direction (in vs out), blocking traffic that should be permitted

title: NAT Pool Exhausted
symptom: During peak hours, some internal users lose internet access while others remain connected.
topology_note: Router1 uses a NAT pool (not overload) for translating internal addresses.
show_output:
show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 20 (20 static, 0 dynamic; 0 extended)
Pool NAT-POOL: netmask 255.255.255.240
 start 203.0.113.10 end 203.0.113.20
 total addresses 11 allocated 11 (100%) misses 47
expected_fault: NAT pool has too few public addresses for the number of internal hosts needing translation

title: Wireless Channel Overlap Causing Slow Speeds
symptom: Wi-Fi in the office is connected but extremely slow and drops frequently during business hours.
topology_note: Three APs (AP1, AP2, AP3) cover adjacent areas of the same floor.
show_output:
AP1 channel: 6
AP2 channel: 6
AP3 channel: 6
(all APs using the same 2.4GHz channel, high co-channel interference)
expected_fault: All access points configured on the same overlapping Wi-Fi channel causing interference

title: Missing Default Route on Edge Router
symptom: Internal users can reach all internal subnets but nothing on the internet, even though NAT is configured correctly.
topology_note: Router1 edge router connects to ISP via Serial0/1/0.
show_output:
show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set
C 192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
C 203.0.113.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/1/0
(no default route / 0.0.0.0/0 entry)
expected_fault: No default route (0.0.0.0/0) configured pointing to the ISP, so router drops all internet-bound traffic

title: Port Security Shutting Down Access Port
symptom: PC in the lab suddenly lost network connectivity after being moved to a different desk.
topology_note: Fa0/12 has port security configured with a single allowed MAC address (sticky).
show_output:
show port-security interface Fa0/12
Port Security: Enabled
Port Status: Secure-shutdown
Violation Mode: Shutdown
Last Source Address:Vlan: 00AA.11BB.22CC:10
expected_fault: Port security violation triggered err-disable state after a new device's MAC address appeared on the port

title: Incorrect ACL Wildcard Mask
symptom: ACL intended to permit only 192.168.10.0/24 to the server is unexpectedly permitting a much larger range of addresses.
topology_note: ACL 10 applied on the server-facing SVI.
show_output:
show access-lists 10
Standard IP access list 10
 10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.15.255
expected_fault: Wildcard mask 0.0.15.255 is incorrect for a /24 network; should be 0.0.0.255, permitting a much wider range

title: DNS Server Interface Reachability Issue
symptom: All hostname resolution fails company-wide, but internet browsing by IP still works.
topology_note: Internal DNS server (192.168.10.5) is a VM on VLAN 10; recently migrated to a new host.
show_output:
ping 192.168.10.5
Request timed out. (4 attempts)
show ip interface brief on Switch1 -> Fa0/5 (DNS server port) down down
expected_fault: Physical/link-layer issue on the DNS server's switch port after migration, making DNS server unreachable

title: Overlapping Static and DHCP Gateway Values
symptom: Half of the PCs on VLAN 10 can reach the internet, the other half (statically configured) cannot.
topology_note: VLAN 10 default gateway is Router1 SVI at 192.168.10.1.
show_output:
Static PCs ipconfig -> IPv4 Address: 192.168.10.50 /24 Default Gateway: 192.168.10.254
Router1 show ip interface brief -> Vlan10 192.168.10.1 up up
(192.168.10.254 is not assigned to any router interface)
expected_fault: Statically configured PCs point to a non-existent gateway address (192.168.10.254) instead of the router's actual SVI

title: NAT Static Mapping Conflict
symptom: External users cannot reach the internal web server via the public IP, connection resets immediately.
topology_note: Static NAT configured to map public 203.0.113.50 to internal web server 192.168.1.100.
show_output:
show run | include ip nat inside source static
ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.100 203.0.113.50
ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.101 203.0.113.50
expected_fault: Duplicate static NAT mapping - two internal hosts mapped to the same public IP, causing conflict

title: Wireless AP Not Broadcasting SSID
symptom: Employees report that the corporate SSID has disappeared from their device Wi-Fi lists this morning.
topology_note: AP2 covers the second-floor east wing.
show_output:
AP2 config: dot11 ssid CorpWiFi
 broadcast-ssid disabled
(SSID broadcast recently toggled off during a config change)
expected_fault: SSID broadcast was disabled on the access point, hiding the network from normal device scans

title: Route Summarization Blackhole
symptom: A specific branch subnet (172.16.25.0/24) is unreachable while the rest of the branch network works fine.
topology_note: HQ router summarizes branch routes as 172.16.16.0/20 pointing to Branch router.
show_output:
show ip route
O 172.16.16.0/20 [110/65] via 10.0.0.2
(no more-specific route exists for 172.16.25.0/24 at Branch, traffic blackholed after summarization)
expected_fault: Route summarization advertises a supernet that includes an address space not actually present at the branch, creating a routing black hole

title: Incorrect VLAN Assignment on Voice Port
symptom: IP phone registers correctly but the PC connected to the phone's pass-through port cannot get on the data VLAN.
topology_note: Fa0/15 configured for an IP phone with a PC daisy-chained behind it.
show_output:
show run interface Fa0/15
switchport voice vlan 50
(switchport access vlan command missing - port defaults to VLAN 1 for data)
expected_fault: Voice VLAN configured correctly but data VLAN for the access (PC) side was never set, defaulting to VLAN 1

title: Default Gateway on Wrong Subnet
symptom: PCs in VLAN 20 can ping each other but cannot reach their default gateway or any other subnet.
topology_note: VLAN 20 subnet is 192.168.20.0/24. Router1 SVI Vlan20 is 192.168.20.1.
show_output:
ipconfig /all
IPv4 Address: 192.168.20.10
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.30.1
Router1 show ip interface brief -> Vlan20 192.168.20.1 up up
expected_fault: Default gateway (192.168.30.1) is on a different subnet than the host (192.168.20.0/24)

title: Entire DHCP Scope Excluded
symptom: New devices in VLAN 30 cannot get an IP address and fall back to a 169.254.x.x automatic address.
topology_note: Router1 is the DHCP server for VLAN 30 (192.168.30.0/24).
show_output:
show run | section ip dhcp pool VLAN30
 network 192.168.30.0 255.255.255.0
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.30.1 192.168.30.254
(entire pool range excluded - no usable addresses remain)
expected_fault: The DHCP excluded-address range covers the whole scope, leaving no addresses to lease
